predictedRisks.riskTitle: Undocumented 7-week extension may trigger commercial disputes and payment milestone misalignment
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project timeline has implicitly extended from the September 11, 2026 contract end date to October 30, 2026 (Hypercare completion), representing a 43.75% duration increase without formal contract amendment. All critical delivery phases—PAT, code freeze, regression, deployment, and hypercare—are scheduled partially or entirely beyond the original contract baseline. This creates significant commercial ambiguity regarding payment milestone alignment, acceptance criteria, resource commitments, warranty periods, and governance authority for post-contract activities.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Implicit timeline extension introduced through expanded quality gates (15-day PAT, 15-day regression) and sprint-based delivery model without corresponding contract amendment or change order execution.
triggerConditions: PAT phase commences on August 31 without formal extension approval
Payment milestone invoice submitted for post-contract activities without amended payment schedule
Acceptance criteria dispute arises during PAT or regression phases
Resource availability conflicts emerge in October timeframe due to lack of formal commitment

potentialImpact.commercial: Payment disputes, invoice rejection, or delayed payment for 40% of contract value ($96,800) tied to post-contract milestones; potential vendor margin erosion from uncompensated extended resource commitment
potentialImpact.governance: Acceptance criteria ambiguity, warranty period confusion, and unclear escalation authority for post-contract period; risk of contractual disputes requiring legal intervention
potentialImpact.schedule: Resource unavailability in October may force further delays or quality compromises; lack of formal commitment creates execution uncertainty for final 7 weeks

predictedRisks.reasoning: This risk is highly likely because the current project timeline explicitly shows all critical phases extending beyond the September 11 contract end date, with 40% of payment milestones tied to post-contract activities. Historical intelligence confirms this exact pattern occurred previously (R02) and was never effectively resolved through formal baseline control. The combination of implicit extension, lack of documented amendment, and historical recurrence creates critical commercial and governance exposure.
